**Commentary on Surah al-Kawthar (Tafsir, exegesis)**

It is Madani, though it has been said to be Makki.

In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.

* *

Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from al-Mukhtar ibn Fulful, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ dozed off briefly, then raised his head smiling. Either they said to him or he said to them: "Why are you laughing?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "A surah has just been revealed to me." Then he recited: In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. ﴿Indeed, We have granted you al-Kawthar﴾, until he finished it. Then he said: "Do you know what al-Kawthar is?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "It is a river that my Lord, Mighty and Majestic, has given me in Paradise. It has abundant good. My community will come to it on the Day of Resurrection. Its vessels are as numerous as the stars. A servant of them will be pulled away, and I will say: 'My Lord, he is of my community.' It will be said: 'You do not know what they innovated after you.'" [[Al-Musnad (3/102)]]

Thus Imam Ahmad narrated it with this three-person chain and this wording.

It is also reported concerning the description of the Pool (al-Hawd) on the Day of Resurrection that two spouts from heaven pour into it from the river al-Kawthar, and that beside it are vessels as numerous as the stars of the sky. This hadith was also narrated by Muslim, Abu Dawud and al-Nasa'i, through the route of Muhammad ibn Fudayl and Ali ibn Mushir, both from al-Mukhtar ibn Fulful, from Anas. The wording of Muslim is: "While the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was among us in the mosque, he dozed off briefly, then raised his head smiling. We said: 'What made you laugh, O Messenger of Allah?' He said: 'A surah has just been revealed to me,' and he recited: In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. ﴿Indeed, We have granted you al-Kawthar. So pray to your Lord and sacrifice. Indeed, your enemy is the one cut off.﴾ Then he said: 'Do you know what al-Kawthar is?' We said: 'Allah and His Messenger know best.' He said: 'It is a river that my Lord promised me, Mighty and Majestic. It has abundant good. It is a pool to which my community will come on the Day of Resurrection. Its vessels are as numerous as the stars. A servant of them will be pulled away, and I will say: "My Lord, he is of my community." He will say: "You do not know what he innovated after you."'" [[Sahih Muslim, no. (400); Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (4747); Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. (11702).]]

Many of the reciters (qurra') have used this hadith as evidence that this surah is Madani, and many of the jurists (fuqaha') have used it as evidence that the basmalah (the phrase "In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate") is part of the surah and was revealed with it.

As for the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, We have granted you al-Kawthar﴾, this hadith has already mentioned that it is a river in Paradise. Imam Ahmad also narrated it through another route from Anas, saying: Affan narrated to us, Hammad narrated to us, Thabit informed us, from Anas, that he recited this verse, ﴿Indeed, We have granted you al-Kawthar﴾, and said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I was given al-Kawthar. It is a flowing river, not dug out by digging. On its two banks are domes of pearls. I struck my hand into its soil, and its musk was pungent, and its pebbles were pearls." [[Al-Musnad (2/247).]]

Imam Ahmad also said: Muhammad ibn Abi 'Adi narrated to us, from Humayd, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I entered Paradise and I found a river whose two banks were tents of pearls. I struck my hand toward what the water was flowing through, and it was strong musk. I said: 'What is this, O Jibril?' He said: 'This is al-Kawthar which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has given you.'" [[Al-Musnad (3/103).]]

Al-Bukhari narrated it in his Sahih, and Muslim also, from the hadith of Shaiban ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from Qatadah, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: When the Prophet ﷺ was taken up to the heaven, he said: "I came upon a river whose two banks were hollow domes of pearls. I said: 'What is this, O Jibril?' He said: 'This is al-Kawthar.'" This is the wording of al-Bukhari, may Allah have mercy on him. [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4946).]]

Ibn Jarir said: al-Rabi' narrated to us, Ibn Wahb informed us, from Sulayman ibn Hilal, from Sharik ibn Abi Namir, who said: I heard Anas ibn Malik telling us, he said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was taken on the Night Journey, Jibril took him to the lowest heaven, and there he found a river upon which was a palace of pearls and emerald. He went to smell its dust, and it was musk. He said: "O Jibril, what is this river?" He said: "It is al-Kawthar, which your Lord has stored up for you." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (30/207).]]

The hadith of the Night Journey has already been mentioned in the tafsir of Surah al-Isra' (Surah "Subhan"), through the route of Sharik from Anas, from the Prophet ﷺ, and it is recorded in the two Sahihs. [[See: the tafsir of the beginning of Surah al-Isra'.]]

Sa'id narrated from Qatadah, from Anas, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "While I was walking in Paradise, a river appeared to me whose two banks were hollow domes of pearls. The angel who was with me said: 'Do you know what this is? This is al-Kawthar which Allah has given you.' He struck his hand on its earth and brought out musk from its clay." [[Narrated by al-Tabari in his tafsir (30/208) from Bishr, from Yazid, from Sa'id, with this chain.]] Likewise it was narrated by Sulayman ibn Tarkhan, Ma'mar, Hammam and others, from Qatadah, with the same.

Ibn Jarir said: Ahmad ibn Abi Suraij [in A: "Shurayh"] narrated to us, Abu Ayyub al-'Abbasi narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn Sa'd narrated to us, Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah, the nephew of Ibn Shihab, narrated to me, from his father, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked about al-Kawthar, and he said: "It is a river that Allah has given me in Paradise. Its soil is musk, its water is whiter than milk and sweeter than honey. Birds whose necks are like the necks of camels come to it." Abu Bakr said: "O Messenger of Allah, they are indeed luxurious?" He said: "Their eating is more luxurious than them." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (30/209).]]

Ahmad said: Abu Salamah al-Khuza'i narrated to us, al-Laith narrated to us, from Yazid ibn al-Hadi, from 'Abd al-Wahhab, from 'Abd Allah ibn Muslim ibn Shihab, from Anas, that a man said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is al-Kawthar?" He said: "It is a river in Paradise which my Lord has given me. It is indeed whiter than milk and sweeter than honey. In it are birds whose necks are like the necks of camels." 'Umar said: "O Messenger of Allah, they are indeed luxurious?" He said: "Their eating is more luxurious than them, O 'Umar." [[Al-Musnad (3/220).]]

Ibn Jarir narrated it from the hadith of al-Zuhri, from his brother 'Abd Allah, from Anas: that he asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about al-Kawthar, and he mentioned the like of it exactly. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (30/209).]]

Al-Bukhari said: Khalid ibn Yazid al-Kahili narrated to us, Isra'il narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu 'Ubaydah, from 'A'isha, who said: I asked her about the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, We have granted you al-Kawthar﴾. She said: "It is a [great] river given to your Prophet ﷺ. Its two banks are of hollow pearls, and its vessels are as numerous as the stars." [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4965).]]

Then al-Bukhari said: Zakariyya, Abu al-Ahwas and Mutarrif narrated it from Abu Ishaq.

Ahmad and al-Nasa'i also narrated it through the route of Mutarrif, with the same. [[Al-Musnad (6/81) and Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. (11705).]]

Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan and Isra'il, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu 'Ubaydah, from 'A'isha, who said: "al-Kawthar is a river in Paradise, whose two banks are hollow pearls." Isra'il said: "A river in Paradise, upon which are vessels as numerous as the stars of the sky."

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, Ya'qub al-Qummi narrated to us [in A: "al-'Amma"], from Hafs ibn Humayd, from Shamir ibn 'Atiyyah, from Shaqiq [in A: "Sufyan"] or Masruq, who said: I said to 'A'isha: "O Mother of the Believers, tell me about al-Kawthar." She said: "It is a river in the middle of Paradise (buṭnān al-jannah). Its two banks are palaces of pearl and ruby, its soil is musk, and its pebbles are pearl and ruby."

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Waki' narrated to us, from Abu Ja'far al-Razi, from Ibn Abi Najih, from 'A'isha, who said: "Whoever wishes to hear the roar of al-Kawthar, let him put his two fingers in his ears." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (30/207); Ibn Abi al-Dunya narrated it in Sifat al-Jannah, no. (67), through the route of Muhammad ibn Rabi'ah, from Abu Ja'far al-Razi, from Mujahid, from 'A'isha, in marfu' form.]]

This report is discontinuous (munqati') between Ibn Abi Najih and 'A'isha. In some of the transmissions it reads: "from a man, from her." The meaning of this is that one hears something similar to that, not that one hears it itself. And Allah knows best.

Al-Suhayli said: al-Daraqutni narrated it in marfu' form, through the route of Malik ibn Mighwal [in M: "Yazid ibn Mighwal"], from al-Sha'bi, from Masruq, from 'A'isha, from the Prophet ﷺ. [[Al-Rawd al-Anf of al-Suhayli (1/241).]]

Then al-Bukhari said: Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Hushaym narrated to us, Abu Bishr informed us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, that he said concerning al-Kawthar: "It is the good which Allah has given him." Abu Bishr said: I said to Sa'id ibn Jubayr: "Some people claim it is a river in Paradise?" Sa'id said: "The river in Paradise is of the good which Allah has given him." [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4966).]]

He also narrated it through the hadith of Hushaym, from Abu Bishr and 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "al-Kawthar: abundant good." [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (6578).]]

[Al-Thawri said, from 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "al-Kawthar: abundant good."] [[Addition from Tafsir al-Tabari (30/207).]]

This interpretation includes the river and other things, because al-Kawthar derives from abundance (kathrah), and it is abundant good. The river is among it, as said by Ibn 'Abbas, 'Ikrimah, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Mujahid, Muharib ibn Dithar and al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Hasan al-Basri. Mujahid even said: "It is abundant good in this world and the Hereafter."

'Ikrimah said: "It is prophethood and the Qur'an, and the reward of the Hereafter."

It is also authentically reported from Ibn 'Abbas that he explained it as the river as well. Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, 'Umar ibn 'Ubayd narrated to us, from 'Ata', from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "al-Kawthar: a river in Paradise, whose two banks are gold and silver, flowing over ruby and pearl. Its water is whiter than snow and sweeter than honey."

Al-'Awfi narrated something similar from Ibn 'Abbas.

Ibn Jarir said: Ya'qub narrated to me, Hushaym narrated to us, 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib informed us, from Muharib ibn Dithar, from Ibn 'Umar, that he said: "al-Kawthar is a river in Paradise, whose two banks are gold and silver, flowing over pearl and ruby. Its water is far whiter than milk and sweeter than honey."

Likewise al-Tirmidhi narrated it from Ibn Humayd, from Jarir, from 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, with the same, as a statement of a Companion (mawquf). [[Tafsir al-Tabari (30/207). I have not found it in the Sunan of al-Tirmidhi by this route, nor did al-Mizzi mention it in Tuhfat al-Ashraf.]] It has also been reported in marfu' form. Imam Ahmad said:

Ali ibn Hafs narrated to us, Warqa' narrated to us, who said ... and 'Ata' [ibn al-Sa'ib] [addition from M] said, from Muharib ibn Dithar, from Ibn 'Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "al-Kawthar is a river in Paradise, whose two banks are of gold, and the water flows over pearl. Its water is far whiter than milk and sweeter than honey."

This is how al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir narrated it, through the route of Muhammad ibn Fudayl, from 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, with it in marfu' form. [[Al-Musnad (2/158); Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (3361); Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (4334); Tafsir al-Tabari (30/210).]] Al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan sahih."

Ibn Jarir said: Yaqub related to me, Ibn Ulayyah related to us, 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib informed us, saying: Muharib ibn Dithar said to me: "What did Sa'id ibn Jubayr say about al-Kawthar?" I said: "He related to us from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: It is the abundant good." He said: "He spoke the truth; by Allah, it is indeed abundant good. But Ibn 'Umar related to us that he said: When the verse ﴿Indeed, We have granted you al-Kawthar﴾ was revealed, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'al-Kawthar is a river in Paradise, whose banks are of gold, flowing over pearls and rubies.'" [[Tafsir al-Tabari (30/210).]]

Ibn Jarir said: Harun ibn Ishaq related to me, Ibn Abi Maryam related to us, Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn Abi Kathir related to us, Haram ibn 'Uthman informed me, from 'Abd al-Rahman al-A'raj, from Usamah ibn Zayd: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came one day to Hamzah ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib and did not find him, so he asked his wife about him—she was from the Banu al-Najjar—and she said: "O Prophet of Allah, he just went out intending to come to you, and I think he missed you in some of the alleys of the Banu al-Najjar. Will you not enter, O Messenger of Allah?" So he entered, and she brought him a dish of hays, and he ate some of it. She said: "O Messenger of Allah, may it be wholesome and pleasant for you! You came while I was about to come to you to congratulate you and to bring you joy. Abu 'Umarah informed me that you were given a river in Paradise called al-Kawthar." He said: "Indeed, and its expanse—that is, its land—is of rubies, coral, chrysolite and pearls." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (30/210).]]

Haram ibn 'Uthman is weak. However, this context is good, and the basis of this has been authenticated; indeed it has been transmitted through a chain that, according to many of the imams of hadith, yields certainty. Likewise are the hadiths of the Pool [and let us mention them here]. [[An addition from A, and so the Hafiz said; the mention of the hadiths of the Pool does not occur in the copies, but Hafiz Ibn Kathir mentioned them in his book (al-Nihayah fi al-Fitan wa al-Malahim 1/374-412), and were it not for fear of lengthiness we would have mentioned them here, so let it be referred to there.]]

Thus it has been narrated from Anas, Abu al-'Aliyah, Mujahid, and other than one of the early generation (salaf) that al-Kawthar is a river in Paradise. 'Ata' said: it is a pool in Paradise.

* *

His saying: ﴿So pray to your Lord and sacrifice﴾ means: just as We have granted you abundant good in this world and the Hereafter, of which that river whose description has preceded is part—so devote your obligatory prayer and your voluntary prayer to your Lord, and your sacrifice; worship Him alone, with no partner, and sacrifice in His name alone, with no partner. As He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Say: Indeed, my prayer, my rites, my living and my dying are for Allah, Lord of the worlds. He has no partner. And that I have been commanded, and I am the first of the Muslims﴾ [al-An'am: 162-163]. Ibn 'Abbas, 'Ata', Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, and al-Hasan said: this means the sacrifice of camels and the like. Likewise said Qatadah, Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, al-Dahhak, al-Rabi', 'Ata' al-Khurasani, al-Hakam, and Isma'il [in M: "and Sa'id"] ibn Abi Khalid, and other than one of the early generation. This is in contrast to what the polytheists were upon of prostrating to other than Allah and slaughtering in the name of other than Him, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And do not eat of that over which the name of Allah has not been mentioned, for indeed it is grave disobedience﴾ — the verse [al-An'am: 121].

It has been said: what is meant by His saying ﴿and sacrifice﴾ is placing the right hand upon the left beneath the chest (nahr). This is narrated from 'Ali, but it is not authentic. Similarly from al-Sha'bi.

And from Abu Ja'far al-Baqir: ﴿and sacrifice﴾ means: raise the hands at the beginning of the prayer.

It has been said: ﴿and sacrifice﴾ means: face the qiblah with your chest. Ibn Jarir mentioned these three views.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated here a extremely odd hadith, saying: Wahb ibn Ibrahim al-Fami [in A: "al-'Ami"] related to us—in the year 255 AH—Isra'il ibn Hatim al-Marwazi related to us, Muqatil ibn Hayyan related to us, from al-Asbagh ibn Nubatah, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, who said: When this surah was revealed upon the Prophet ﷺ: ﴿Indeed, We have granted you al-Kawthar. So pray to your Lord and sacrifice﴾, the Messenger of Allah said: "O Jibril, what is this sacrifice (nahirah) which my Lord has commanded me with?" He said: "It is not a sacrifice, but He commands you, when you begin the prayer, to raise your hands when you say the takbir, when you bow, when you raise your head from bowing, and when you prostrate, for this is our prayer and the prayer of the angels who are in the seven heavens; and indeed for everything there is an adornment, and the adornment of the prayer is raising the hands at every takbir."

Likewise it was narrated by al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak, from the hadith of Isra'il ibn Hatim, with it. [[al-Mustadrak (2/537); he narrated it also through al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan (2/75); and Ibn Hibban narrated it in al-Majruhin (1/177) through Isra'il ibn Hatim, with it. Ibn Hibban said: "This text is false, except the mention of raising the hands in it; this report was narrated by 'Umar ibn Subh, from Muqatil ibn Hayyan, and 'Umar ibn Subh fabricates hadith, so Isra'il ibn Hatim took advantage of it and narrated it from Muqatil."]]

From 'Ata' al-Khurasani: ﴿and sacrifice﴾ means: raise your back after bowing and stand upright, and expose your chest, meaning by it standing upright (i'tidal). Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim.

[All these views are very odd.] [[An addition from M and A.]] The correct view is the first, that the sacrifice (nahr) means slaughtering the rites (manasik). For this reason the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pray the 'Id and then sacrifice his offering, and he would say: "Whoever prays our prayer and performs our sacrifice, he has done the sacrifice correctly. And whoever sacrifices before the prayer, there is no sacrifice for him." Abu Burdah ibn Niyar stood and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I sacrificed my sheep before the prayer, and I knew that today is a day when meat is desired." He said: "Your sheep is a sheep of meat." He said: "But I have a young female goat (inaq) which is dearer to me than two sheep; will it suffice for me?" He said: "It will suffice you, but it will not suffice anyone after you." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. (983), from the hadith of al-Bara', may Allah be pleased with him.]]

Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir said: The correct view is the statement of the one who said: the meaning of that is: make your entire prayer sincerely for your Lord, to the exclusion of whatever else of rivals and deities [in M: "and children"]; and likewise make your sacrifice for Him alone, to the exclusion of idols; in gratitude to Him for the honour and good which He has given you, which has no equal, and with which He has singled you out. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (30/212).]]

What he said is in the utmost excellence, and Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi and 'Ata' had preceded him to this meaning.

* *

His saying: ﴿Indeed, your hater—he is the one cut off (al-abtar)﴾ means: indeed your hater—O Muhammad—and the hater of what you have brought of guidance, truth, clear proof, shining light and manifest illumination, he is the abtar: the most humble, the most debased, whose remembrance is cut off.

Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, and Qatadah said: it was revealed concerning al-'As ibn Wa'il.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said, from Yazid ibn Ruman, who said: Whenever al-'As ibn Wa'il mentioned the Messenger of Allah ﷺ he would say: "Leave him, for he is an abtar man with no offspring; when he dies, his remembrance will be cut off." So Allah revealed this surah.

Shamir ibn 'Atiyyah said: it was revealed concerning 'Uqbah ibn Abi Mu'ayt.

Ibn 'Abbas also said, as did 'Ikrimah: it was revealed concerning Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf and a group of the disbelievers of Quraysh.

al-Bazzar said: Ziyad ibn Yahya al-Hassani related to us, Ibn Abi 'Adi related to us, from Dawud, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas who said: Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf came to Makkah, and Quraysh said to him: "You are their chief; do you not see this sabir (cut-off one) [in M: 'al-dabr'], the one cut off from his people, who claims he is better than us, while we are the people of the pilgrimage, the keepers of the Ka'bah (sidanah), and the people of the water-providing (siqayah)?" He said: "You are better than him." So it was revealed: ﴿Indeed, your hater—he is the one cut off﴾.

Thus al-Bazzar narrated it [[Musnad al-Bazzar no. (2293), Kashf al-Astar; in it occurs: "al-Hasan ibn 'Ali al-Wasiti related to us, Yahya ibn Rashid related to us, from Dawud," and he mentioned the like; al-Nasa'i also narrated it in al-Sunan al-Kubra no. (11707).]] and its chain is sahih.

And from 'Ata': it was revealed concerning Abu Lahab, at the time when the son of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ died, and Abu Lahab went to the polytheists and said: "Muhammad has been cut off tonight." So Allah revealed concerning that: ﴿Indeed, your hater—he is the one cut off﴾.

And from Ibn 'Abbas: it was revealed concerning Abu Jahl. And from him: ﴿Indeed, your hater﴾ means: your enemy. This encompasses all who are characterized by this among those mentioned, and others.

'Ikrimah said: al-abtar means: the solitary one. al-Suddi said: when a man's male children died, they would say: "He has been cut off." When the sons of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ died, they said: "Muhammad has been cut off." So Allah revealed: ﴿Indeed, your hater—he is the one cut off﴾.

This returns to what we have said, that the abtar is the one whose remembrance is cut off when he dies; they imagined, in their ignorance, that if his sons die, his remembrance is cut off. Far from it, by no means! Rather, Allah has preserved his remembrance upon the heads of witnesses, and has made his law obligatory upon the necks of the servants, continuing through the perpetuity of eternity, until the Day of Gathering and Return, [in M: "and the Day of Calling out"] — the blessings of Allah and His peace be upon him always until the Day of Calling out.

End of the tafsir of Surah "al-Kawthar", and to Allah belongs all praise and grace.

**Commentary on Surah al-Kawthar (Tafsir, exegesis)**

It is Madani, though it has been said to be Makki.

In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.

* *

Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from al-Mukhtar ibn Fulful, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ dozed off briefly, then raised his head smiling. Either they said to him or he said to them: "Why are you laughing?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "A surah has just been revealed to me." Then he recited: In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. ﴿Indeed, We have granted you al-Kawthar﴾, until he finished it. Then he said: "Do you know what al-Kawthar is?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "It is a river that my Lord, Mighty and Majestic, has given me in Paradise. It has abundant good. My community will come to it on the Day of Resurrection. Its vessels are as numerous as the stars. A servant of them will be pulled away, and I will say: 'My Lord, he is of my community.' It will be said: 'You do not know what they innovated after you.'" [[Al-Musnad (3/102)]]

Thus Imam Ahmad narrated it with this three-person chain and this wording.

It is also reported concerning the description of the Pool (al-Hawd) on the Day of Resurrection that two spouts from heaven pour into it from the river al-Kawthar, and that beside it are vessels as numerous as the stars of the sky. This hadith was also narrated by Muslim, Abu Dawud and al-Nasa'i, through the route of Muhammad ibn Fudayl and Ali ibn Mushir, both from al-Mukhtar ibn Fulful, from Anas. The wording of Muslim is: "While the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was among us in the mosque, he dozed off briefly, then raised his head smiling. We said: 'What made you laugh, O Messenger of Allah?' He said: 'A surah has just been revealed to me,' and he recited: In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. ﴿Indeed, We have granted you al-Kawthar. So pray to your Lord and sacrifice. Indeed, your enemy is the one cut off.﴾ Then he said: 'Do you know what al-Kawthar is?' We said: 'Allah and His Messenger know best.' He said: 'It is a river that my Lord promised me, Mighty and Majestic. It has abundant good. It is a pool to which my community will come on the Day of Resurrection. Its vessels are as numerous as the stars. A servant of them will be pulled away, and I will say: "My Lord, he is of my community." He will say: "You do not know what he innovated after you."'" [[Sahih Muslim, no. (400); Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (4747); Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. (11702).]]

Many of the reciters (qurra') have used this hadith as evidence that this surah is Madani, and many of the jurists (fuqaha') have used it as evidence that the basmalah (the phrase "In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate") is part of the surah and was revealed with it.

As for the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, We have granted you al-Kawthar﴾, this hadith has already mentioned that it is a river in Paradise. Imam Ahmad also narrated it through another route from Anas, saying: Affan narrated to us, Hammad narrated to us, Thabit informed us, from Anas, that he recited this verse, ﴿Indeed, We have granted you al-Kawthar﴾, and said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I was given al-Kawthar. It is a flowing river, not dug out by digging. On its two banks are domes of pearls. I struck my hand into its soil, and its musk was pungent, and its pebbles were pearls." [[Al-Musnad (2/247).]]

Imam Ahmad also said: Muhammad ibn Abi 'Adi narrated to us, from Humayd, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I entered Paradise and I found a river whose two banks were tents of pearls. I struck my hand toward what the water was flowing through, and it was strong musk. I said: 'What is this, O Jibril?' He said: 'This is al-Kawthar which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has given you.'" [[Al-Musnad (3/103).]]

Al-Bukhari narrated it in his Sahih, and Muslim also, from the hadith of Shaiban ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from Qatadah, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: When the Prophet ﷺ was taken up to the heaven, he said: "I came upon a river whose two banks were hollow domes of pearls. I said: 'What is this, O Jibril?' He said: 'This is al-Kawthar.'" This is the wording of al-Bukhari, may Allah have mercy on him. [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4946).]]

Ibn Jarir said: al-Rabi' narrated to us, Ibn Wahb informed us, from Sulayman ibn Hilal, from Sharik ibn Abi Namir, who said: I heard Anas ibn Malik telling us, he said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was taken on the Night Journey, Jibril took him to the lowest heaven, and there he found a river upon which was a palace of pearls and emerald. He went to smell its dust, and it was musk. He said: "O Jibril, what is this river?" He said: "It is al-Kawthar, which your Lord has stored up for you." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (30/207).]]

The hadith of the Night Journey has already been mentioned in the tafsir of Surah al-Isra' (Surah "Subhan"), through the route of Sharik from Anas, from the Prophet ﷺ, and it is recorded in the two Sahihs. [[See: the tafsir of the beginning of Surah al-Isra'.]]

Sa'id narrated from Qatadah, from Anas, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "While I was walking in Paradise, a river appeared to me whose two banks were hollow domes of pearls. The angel who was with me said: 'Do you know what this is? This is al-Kawthar which Allah has given you.' He struck his hand on its earth and brought out musk from its clay." [[Narrated by al-Tabari in his tafsir (30/208) from Bishr, from Yazid, from Sa'id, with this chain.]] Likewise it was narrated by Sulayman ibn Tarkhan, Ma'mar, Hammam and others, from Qatadah, with the same.

Ibn Jarir said: Ahmad ibn Abi Suraij [in A: "Shurayh"] narrated to us, Abu Ayyub al-'Abbasi narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn Sa'd narrated to us, Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah, the nephew of Ibn Shihab, narrated to me, from his father, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked about al-Kawthar, and he said: "It is a river that Allah has given me in Paradise. Its soil is musk, its water is whiter than milk and sweeter than honey. Birds whose necks are like the necks of camels come to it." Abu Bakr said: "O Messenger of Allah, they are indeed luxurious?" He said: "Their eating is more luxurious than them." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (30/209).]]

Ahmad said: Abu Salamah al-Khuza'i narrated to us, al-Laith narrated to us, from Yazid ibn al-Hadi, from 'Abd al-Wahhab, from 'Abd Allah ibn Muslim ibn Shihab, from Anas, that a man said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is al-Kawthar?" He said: "It is a river in Paradise which my Lord has given me. It is indeed whiter than milk and sweeter than honey. In it are birds whose necks are like the necks of camels." 'Umar said: "O Messenger of Allah, they are indeed luxurious?" He said: "Their eating is more luxurious than them, O 'Umar." [[Al-Musnad (3/220).]]

Ibn Jarir narrated it from the hadith of al-Zuhri, from his brother 'Abd Allah, from Anas: that he asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about al-Kawthar, and he mentioned the like of it exactly. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (30/209).]]

Al-Bukhari said: Khalid ibn Yazid al-Kahili narrated to us, Isra'il narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu 'Ubaydah, from 'A'isha, who said: I asked her about the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, We have granted you al-Kawthar﴾. She said: "It is a [great] river given to your Prophet ﷺ. Its two banks are of hollow pearls, and its vessels are as numerous as the stars." [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4965).]]

Then al-Bukhari said: Zakariyya, Abu al-Ahwas and Mutarrif narrated it from Abu Ishaq.

Ahmad and al-Nasa'i also narrated it through the route of Mutarrif, with the same. [[Al-Musnad (6/81) and Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. (11705).]]

Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan and Isra'il, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu 'Ubaydah, from 'A'isha, who said: "al-Kawthar is a river in Paradise, whose two banks are hollow pearls." Isra'il said: "A river in Paradise, upon which are vessels as numerous as the stars of the sky."

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, Ya'qub al-Qummi narrated to us [in A: "al-'Amma"], from Hafs ibn Humayd, from Shamir ibn 'Atiyyah, from Shaqiq [in A: "Sufyan"] or Masruq, who said: I said to 'A'isha: "O Mother of the Believers, tell me about al-Kawthar." She said: "It is a river in the middle of Paradise (buṭnān al-jannah). Its two banks are palaces of pearl and ruby, its soil is musk, and its pebbles are pearl and ruby."

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Waki' narrated to us, from Abu Ja'far al-Razi, from Ibn Abi Najih, from 'A'isha, who said: "Whoever wishes to hear the roar of al-Kawthar, let him put his two fingers in his ears." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (30/207); Ibn Abi al-Dunya narrated it in Sifat al-Jannah, no. (67), through the route of Muhammad ibn Rabi'ah, from Abu Ja'far al-Razi, from Mujahid, from 'A'isha, in marfu' form.]]

This report is discontinuous (munqati') between Ibn Abi Najih and 'A'isha. In some of the transmissions it reads: "from a man, from her." The meaning of this is that one hears something similar to that, not that one hears it itself. And Allah knows best.

Al-Suhayli said: al-Daraqutni narrated it in marfu' form, through the route of Malik ibn Mighwal [in M: "Yazid ibn Mighwal"], from al-Sha'bi, from Masruq, from 'A'isha, from the Prophet ﷺ. [[Al-Rawd al-Anf of al-Suhayli (1/241).]]

Then al-Bukhari said: Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Hushaym narrated to us, Abu Bishr informed us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, that he said concerning al-Kawthar: "It is the good which Allah has given him." Abu Bishr said: I said to Sa'id ibn Jubayr: "Some people claim it is a river in Paradise?" Sa'id said: "The river in Paradise is of the good which Allah has given him." [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4966).]]

He also narrated it through the hadith of Hushaym, from Abu Bishr and 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "al-Kawthar: abundant good." [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (6578).]]

[Al-Thawri said, from 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "al-Kawthar: abundant good."] [[Addition from Tafsir al-Tabari (30/207).]]

This interpretation includes the river and other things, because al-Kawthar derives from abundance (kathrah), and it is abundant good. The river is among it, as said by Ibn 'Abbas, 'Ikrimah, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Mujahid, Muharib ibn Dithar and al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Hasan al-Basri. Mujahid even said: "It is abundant good in this world and the Hereafter."

'Ikrimah said: "It is prophethood and the Qur'an, and the reward of the Hereafter."

It is also authentically reported from Ibn 'Abbas that he explained it as the river as well. Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, 'Umar ibn 'Ubayd narrated to us, from 'Ata', from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "al-Kawthar: a river in Paradise, whose two banks are gold and silver, flowing over ruby and pearl. Its water is whiter than snow and sweeter than honey."

Al-'Awfi narrated something similar from Ibn 'Abbas.

Ibn Jarir said: Ya'qub narrated to me, Hushaym narrated to us, 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib informed us, from Muharib ibn Dithar, from Ibn 'Umar, that he said: "al-Kawthar is a river in Paradise, whose two banks are gold and silver, flowing over pearl and ruby. Its water is far whiter than milk and sweeter than honey."

Likewise al-Tirmidhi narrated it from Ibn Humayd, from Jarir, from 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, with the same, as a statement of a Companion (mawquf). [[Tafsir al-Tabari (30/207). I have not found it in the Sunan of al-Tirmidhi by this route, nor did al-Mizzi mention it in Tuhfat al-Ashraf.]] It has also been reported in marfu' form. Imam Ahmad said:

Ali ibn Hafs narrated to us, Warqa' narrated to us, who said ... and 'Ata' [ibn al-Sa'ib] [addition from M] said, from Muharib ibn Dithar, from Ibn 'Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "al-Kawthar is a river in Paradise, whose two banks are of gold, and the water flows over pearl. Its water is far whiter than milk and sweeter than honey."

This is how al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir narrated it, through the route of Muhammad ibn Fudayl, from 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, with it in marfu' form. [[Al-Musnad (2/158); Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (3361); Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (4334); Tafsir al-Tabari (30/210).]] Al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan sahih."

Ibn Jarir said: Yaqub related to me, Ibn Ulayyah related to us, 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib informed us, saying: Muharib ibn Dithar said to me: "What did Sa'id ibn Jubayr say about al-Kawthar?" I said: "He related to us from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: It is the abundant good." He said: "He spoke the truth; by Allah, it is indeed abundant good. But Ibn 'Umar related to us that he said: When the verse ﴿Indeed, We have granted you al-Kawthar﴾ was revealed, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'al-Kawthar is a river in Paradise, whose banks are of gold, flowing over pearls and rubies.'" [[Tafsir al-Tabari (30/210).]]

Ibn Jarir said: Harun ibn Ishaq related to me, Ibn Abi Maryam related to us, Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn Abi Kathir related to us, Haram ibn 'Uthman informed me, from 'Abd al-Rahman al-A'raj, from Usamah ibn Zayd: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came one day to Hamzah ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib and did not find him, so he asked his wife about him—she was from the Banu al-Najjar—and she said: "O Prophet of Allah, he just went out intending to come to you, and I think he missed you in some of the alleys of the Banu al-Najjar. Will you not enter, O Messenger of Allah?" So he entered, and she brought him a dish of hays, and he ate some of it. She said: "O Messenger of Allah, may it be wholesome and pleasant for you! You came while I was about to come to you to congratulate you and to bring you joy. Abu 'Umarah informed me that you were given a river in Paradise called al-Kawthar." He said: "Indeed, and its expanse—that is, its land—is of rubies, coral, chrysolite and pearls." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (30/210).]]

Haram ibn 'Uthman is weak. However, this context is good, and the basis of this has been authenticated; indeed it has been transmitted through a chain that, according to many of the imams of hadith, yields certainty. Likewise are the hadiths of the Pool [and let us mention them here]. [[An addition from A, and so the Hafiz said; the mention of the hadiths of the Pool does not occur in the copies, but Hafiz Ibn Kathir mentioned them in his book (al-Nihayah fi al-Fitan wa al-Malahim 1/374-412), and were it not for fear of lengthiness we would have mentioned them here, so let it be referred to there.]]

Thus it has been narrated from Anas, Abu al-'Aliyah, Mujahid, and other than one of the early generation (salaf) that al-Kawthar is a river in Paradise. 'Ata' said: it is a pool in Paradise.

* *

His saying: ﴿So pray to your Lord and sacrifice﴾ means: just as We have granted you abundant good in this world and the Hereafter, of which that river whose description has preceded is part—so devote your obligatory prayer and your voluntary prayer to your Lord, and your sacrifice; worship Him alone, with no partner, and sacrifice in His name alone, with no partner. As He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Say: Indeed, my prayer, my rites, my living and my dying are for Allah, Lord of the worlds. He has no partner. And that I have been commanded, and I am the first of the Muslims﴾ [al-An'am: 162-163]. Ibn 'Abbas, 'Ata', Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, and al-Hasan said: this means the sacrifice of camels and the like. Likewise said Qatadah, Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, al-Dahhak, al-Rabi', 'Ata' al-Khurasani, al-Hakam, and Isma'il [in M: "and Sa'id"] ibn Abi Khalid, and other than one of the early generation. This is in contrast to what the polytheists were upon of prostrating to other than Allah and slaughtering in the name of other than Him, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And do not eat of that over which the name of Allah has not been mentioned, for indeed it is grave disobedience﴾ — the verse [al-An'am: 121].

It has been said: what is meant by His saying ﴿and sacrifice﴾ is placing the right hand upon the left beneath the chest (nahr). This is narrated from 'Ali, but it is not authentic. Similarly from al-Sha'bi.

And from Abu Ja'far al-Baqir: ﴿and sacrifice﴾ means: raise the hands at the beginning of the prayer.

It has been said: ﴿and sacrifice﴾ means: face the qiblah with your chest. Ibn Jarir mentioned these three views.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated here a extremely odd hadith, saying: Wahb ibn Ibrahim al-Fami [in A: "al-'Ami"] related to us—in the year 255 AH—Isra'il ibn Hatim al-Marwazi related to us, Muqatil ibn Hayyan related to us, from al-Asbagh ibn Nubatah, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, who said: When this surah was revealed upon the Prophet ﷺ: ﴿Indeed, We have granted you al-Kawthar. So pray to your Lord and sacrifice﴾, the Messenger of Allah said: "O Jibril, what is this sacrifice (nahirah) which my Lord has commanded me with?" He said: "It is not a sacrifice, but He commands you, when you begin the prayer, to raise your hands when you say the takbir, when you bow, when you raise your head from bowing, and when you prostrate, for this is our prayer and the prayer of the angels who are in the seven heavens; and indeed for everything there is an adornment, and the adornment of the prayer is raising the hands at every takbir."

Likewise it was narrated by al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak, from the hadith of Isra'il ibn Hatim, with it. [[al-Mustadrak (2/537); he narrated it also through al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan (2/75); and Ibn Hibban narrated it in al-Majruhin (1/177) through Isra'il ibn Hatim, with it. Ibn Hibban said: "This text is false, except the mention of raising the hands in it; this report was narrated by 'Umar ibn Subh, from Muqatil ibn Hayyan, and 'Umar ibn Subh fabricates hadith, so Isra'il ibn Hatim took advantage of it and narrated it from Muqatil."]]

From 'Ata' al-Khurasani: ﴿and sacrifice﴾ means: raise your back after bowing and stand upright, and expose your chest, meaning by it standing upright (i'tidal). Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim.

[All these views are very odd.] [[An addition from M and A.]] The correct view is the first, that the sacrifice (nahr) means slaughtering the rites (manasik). For this reason the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pray the 'Id and then sacrifice his offering, and he would say: "Whoever prays our prayer and performs our sacrifice, he has done the sacrifice correctly. And whoever sacrifices before the prayer, there is no sacrifice for him." Abu Burdah ibn Niyar stood and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I sacrificed my sheep before the prayer, and I knew that today is a day when meat is desired." He said: "Your sheep is a sheep of meat." He said: "But I have a young female goat (inaq) which is dearer to me than two sheep; will it suffice for me?" He said: "It will suffice you, but it will not suffice anyone after you." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. (983), from the hadith of al-Bara', may Allah be pleased with him.]]

Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir said: The correct view is the statement of the one who said: the meaning of that is: make your entire prayer sincerely for your Lord, to the exclusion of whatever else of rivals and deities [in M: "and children"]; and likewise make your sacrifice for Him alone, to the exclusion of idols; in gratitude to Him for the honour and good which He has given you, which has no equal, and with which He has singled you out. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (30/212).]]

What he said is in the utmost excellence, and Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi and 'Ata' had preceded him to this meaning.

* *

His saying: ﴿Indeed, your hater—he is the one cut off (al-abtar)﴾ means: indeed your hater—O Muhammad—and the hater of what you have brought of guidance, truth, clear proof, shining light and manifest illumination, he is the abtar: the most humble, the most debased, whose remembrance is cut off.

Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, and Qatadah said: it was revealed concerning al-'As ibn Wa'il.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said, from Yazid ibn Ruman, who said: Whenever al-'As ibn Wa'il mentioned the Messenger of Allah ﷺ he would say: "Leave him, for he is an abtar man with no offspring; when he dies, his remembrance will be cut off." So Allah revealed this surah.

Shamir ibn 'Atiyyah said: it was revealed concerning 'Uqbah ibn Abi Mu'ayt.

Ibn 'Abbas also said, as did 'Ikrimah: it was revealed concerning Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf and a group of the disbelievers of Quraysh.

al-Bazzar said: Ziyad ibn Yahya al-Hassani related to us, Ibn Abi 'Adi related to us, from Dawud, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas who said: Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf came to Makkah, and Quraysh said to him: "You are their chief; do you not see this sabir (cut-off one) [in M: 'al-dabr'], the one cut off from his people, who claims he is better than us, while we are the people of the pilgrimage, the keepers of the Ka'bah (sidanah), and the people of the water-providing (siqayah)?" He said: "You are better than him." So it was revealed: ﴿Indeed, your hater—he is the one cut off﴾.

Thus al-Bazzar narrated it [[Musnad al-Bazzar no. (2293), Kashf al-Astar; in it occurs: "al-Hasan ibn 'Ali al-Wasiti related to us, Yahya ibn Rashid related to us, from Dawud," and he mentioned the like; al-Nasa'i also narrated it in al-Sunan al-Kubra no. (11707).]] and its chain is sahih.

And from 'Ata': it was revealed concerning Abu Lahab, at the time when the son of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ died, and Abu Lahab went to the polytheists and said: "Muhammad has been cut off tonight." So Allah revealed concerning that: ﴿Indeed, your hater—he is the one cut off﴾.

And from Ibn 'Abbas: it was revealed concerning Abu Jahl. And from him: ﴿Indeed, your hater﴾ means: your enemy. This encompasses all who are characterized by this among those mentioned, and others.

'Ikrimah said: al-abtar means: the solitary one. al-Suddi said: when a man's male children died, they would say: "He has been cut off." When the sons of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ died, they said: "Muhammad has been cut off." So Allah revealed: ﴿Indeed, your hater—he is the one cut off﴾.

This returns to what we have said, that the abtar is the one whose remembrance is cut off when he dies; they imagined, in their ignorance, that if his sons die, his remembrance is cut off. Far from it, by no means! Rather, Allah has preserved his remembrance upon the heads of witnesses, and has made his law obligatory upon the necks of the servants, continuing through the perpetuity of eternity, until the Day of Gathering and Return, [in M: "and the Day of Calling out"] — the blessings of Allah and His peace be upon him always until the Day of Calling out.

End of the tafsir of Surah "al-Kawthar", and to Allah belongs all praise and grace.

**Commentary on Surah al-Kawthar (Tafsir, exegesis)**

It is Madani, though it has been said to be Makki.

In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.

* *

Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from al-Mukhtar ibn Fulful, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ dozed off briefly, then raised his head smiling. Either they said to him or he said to them: "Why are you laughing?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "A surah has just been revealed to me." Then he recited: In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. ﴿Indeed, We have granted you al-Kawthar﴾, until he finished it. Then he said: "Do you know what al-Kawthar is?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "It is a river that my Lord, Mighty and Majestic, has given me in Paradise. It has abundant good. My community will come to it on the Day of Resurrection. Its vessels are as numerous as the stars. A servant of them will be pulled away, and I will say: 'My Lord, he is of my community.' It will be said: 'You do not know what they innovated after you.'" [[Al-Musnad (3/102)]]

Thus Imam Ahmad narrated it with this three-person chain and this wording.

It is also reported concerning the description of the Pool (al-Hawd) on the Day of Resurrection that two spouts from heaven pour into it from the river al-Kawthar, and that beside it are vessels as numerous as the stars of the sky. This hadith was also narrated by Muslim, Abu Dawud and al-Nasa'i, through the route of Muhammad ibn Fudayl and Ali ibn Mushir, both from al-Mukhtar ibn Fulful, from Anas. The wording of Muslim is: "While the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was among us in the mosque, he dozed off briefly, then raised his head smiling. We said: 'What made you laugh, O Messenger of Allah?' He said: 'A surah has just been revealed to me,' and he recited: In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. ﴿Indeed, We have granted you al-Kawthar. So pray to your Lord and sacrifice. Indeed, your enemy is the one cut off.﴾ Then he said: 'Do you know what al-Kawthar is?' We said: 'Allah and His Messenger know best.' He said: 'It is a river that my Lord promised me, Mighty and Majestic. It has abundant good. It is a pool to which my community will come on the Day of Resurrection. Its vessels are as numerous as the stars. A servant of them will be pulled away, and I will say: "My Lord, he is of my community." He will say: "You do not know what he innovated after you."'" [[Sahih Muslim, no. (400); Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (4747); Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. (11702).]]

Many of the reciters (qurra') have used this hadith as evidence that this surah is Madani, and many of the jurists (fuqaha') have used it as evidence that the basmalah (the phrase "In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate") is part of the surah and was revealed with it.

As for the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, We have granted you al-Kawthar﴾, this hadith has already mentioned that it is a river in Paradise. Imam Ahmad also narrated it through another route from Anas, saying: Affan narrated to us, Hammad narrated to us, Thabit informed us, from Anas, that he recited this verse, ﴿Indeed, We have granted you al-Kawthar﴾, and said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I was given al-Kawthar. It is a flowing river, not dug out by digging. On its two banks are domes of pearls. I struck my hand into its soil, and its musk was pungent, and its pebbles were pearls." [[Al-Musnad (2/247).]]

Imam Ahmad also said: Muhammad ibn Abi 'Adi narrated to us, from Humayd, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I entered Paradise and I found a river whose two banks were tents of pearls. I struck my hand toward what the water was flowing through, and it was strong musk. I said: 'What is this, O Jibril?' He said: 'This is al-Kawthar which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has given you.'" [[Al-Musnad (3/103).]]

Al-Bukhari narrated it in his Sahih, and Muslim also, from the hadith of Shaiban ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from Qatadah, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: When the Prophet ﷺ was taken up to the heaven, he said: "I came upon a river whose two banks were hollow domes of pearls. I said: 'What is this, O Jibril?' He said: 'This is al-Kawthar.'" This is the wording of al-Bukhari, may Allah have mercy on him. [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4946).]]

Ibn Jarir said: al-Rabi' narrated to us, Ibn Wahb informed us, from Sulayman ibn Hilal, from Sharik ibn Abi Namir, who said: I heard Anas ibn Malik telling us, he said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was taken on the Night Journey, Jibril took him to the lowest heaven, and there he found a river upon which was a palace of pearls and emerald. He went to smell its dust, and it was musk. He said: "O Jibril, what is this river?" He said: "It is al-Kawthar, which your Lord has stored up for you." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (30/207).]]

The hadith of the Night Journey has already been mentioned in the tafsir of Surah al-Isra' (Surah "Subhan"), through the route of Sharik from Anas, from the Prophet ﷺ, and it is recorded in the two Sahihs. [[See: the tafsir of the beginning of Surah al-Isra'.]]

Sa'id narrated from Qatadah, from Anas, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "While I was walking in Paradise, a river appeared to me whose two banks were hollow domes of pearls. The angel who was with me said: 'Do you know what this is? This is al-Kawthar which Allah has given you.' He struck his hand on its earth and brought out musk from its clay." [[Narrated by al-Tabari in his tafsir (30/208) from Bishr, from Yazid, from Sa'id, with this chain.]] Likewise it was narrated by Sulayman ibn Tarkhan, Ma'mar, Hammam and others, from Qatadah, with the same.

Ibn Jarir said: Ahmad ibn Abi Suraij [in A: "Shurayh"] narrated to us, Abu Ayyub al-'Abbasi narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn Sa'd narrated to us, Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah, the nephew of Ibn Shihab, narrated to me, from his father, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked about al-Kawthar, and he said: "It is a river that Allah has given me in Paradise. Its soil is musk, its water is whiter than milk and sweeter than honey. Birds whose necks are like the necks of camels come to it." Abu Bakr said: "O Messenger of Allah, they are indeed luxurious?" He said: "Their eating is more luxurious than them." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (30/209).]]

Ahmad said: Abu Salamah al-Khuza'i narrated to us, al-Laith narrated to us, from Yazid ibn al-Hadi, from 'Abd al-Wahhab, from 'Abd Allah ibn Muslim ibn Shihab, from Anas, that a man said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is al-Kawthar?" He said: "It is a river in Paradise which my Lord has given me. It is indeed whiter than milk and sweeter than honey. In it are birds whose necks are like the necks of camels." 'Umar said: "O Messenger of Allah, they are indeed luxurious?" He said: "Their eating is more luxurious than them, O 'Umar." [[Al-Musnad (3/220).]]

Ibn Jarir narrated it from the hadith of al-Zuhri, from his brother 'Abd Allah, from Anas: that he asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about al-Kawthar, and he mentioned the like of it exactly. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (30/209).]]

Al-Bukhari said: Khalid ibn Yazid al-Kahili narrated to us, Isra'il narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu 'Ubaydah, from 'A'isha, who said: I asked her about the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, We have granted you al-Kawthar﴾. She said: "It is a [great] river given to your Prophet ﷺ. Its two banks are of hollow pearls, and its vessels are as numerous as the stars." [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4965).]]

Then al-Bukhari said: Zakariyya, Abu al-Ahwas and Mutarrif narrated it from Abu Ishaq.

Ahmad and al-Nasa'i also narrated it through the route of Mutarrif, with the same. [[Al-Musnad (6/81) and Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. (11705).]]

Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan and Isra'il, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu 'Ubaydah, from 'A'isha, who said: "al-Kawthar is a river in Paradise, whose two banks are hollow pearls." Isra'il said: "A river in Paradise, upon which are vessels as numerous as the stars of the sky."

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, Ya'qub al-Qummi narrated to us [in A: "al-'Amma"], from Hafs ibn Humayd, from Shamir ibn 'Atiyyah, from Shaqiq [in A: "Sufyan"] or Masruq, who said: I said to 'A'isha: "O Mother of the Believers, tell me about al-Kawthar." She said: "It is a river in the middle of Paradise (buṭnān al-jannah). Its two banks are palaces of pearl and ruby, its soil is musk, and its pebbles are pearl and ruby."

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Waki' narrated to us, from Abu Ja'far al-Razi, from Ibn Abi Najih, from 'A'isha, who said: "Whoever wishes to hear the roar of al-Kawthar, let him put his two fingers in his ears." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (30/207); Ibn Abi al-Dunya narrated it in Sifat al-Jannah, no. (67), through the route of Muhammad ibn Rabi'ah, from Abu Ja'far al-Razi, from Mujahid, from 'A'isha, in marfu' form.]]

This report is discontinuous (munqati') between Ibn Abi Najih and 'A'isha. In some of the transmissions it reads: "from a man, from her." The meaning of this is that one hears something similar to that, not that one hears it itself. And Allah knows best.

Al-Suhayli said: al-Daraqutni narrated it in marfu' form, through the route of Malik ibn Mighwal [in M: "Yazid ibn Mighwal"], from al-Sha'bi, from Masruq, from 'A'isha, from the Prophet ﷺ. [[Al-Rawd al-Anf of al-Suhayli (1/241).]]

Then al-Bukhari said: Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Hushaym narrated to us, Abu Bishr informed us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, that he said concerning al-Kawthar: "It is the good which Allah has given him." Abu Bishr said: I said to Sa'id ibn Jubayr: "Some people claim it is a river in Paradise?" Sa'id said: "The river in Paradise is of the good which Allah has given him." [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4966).]]

He also narrated it through the hadith of Hushaym, from Abu Bishr and 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "al-Kawthar: abundant good." [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (6578).]]

[Al-Thawri said, from 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "al-Kawthar: abundant good."] [[Addition from Tafsir al-Tabari (30/207).]]

This interpretation includes the river and other things, because al-Kawthar derives from abundance (kathrah), and it is abundant good. The river is among it, as said by Ibn 'Abbas, 'Ikrimah, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Mujahid, Muharib ibn Dithar and al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Hasan al-Basri. Mujahid even said: "It is abundant good in this world and the Hereafter."

'Ikrimah said: "It is prophethood and the Qur'an, and the reward of the Hereafter."

It is also authentically reported from Ibn 'Abbas that he explained it as the river as well. Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, 'Umar ibn 'Ubayd narrated to us, from 'Ata', from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "al-Kawthar: a river in Paradise, whose two banks are gold and silver, flowing over ruby and pearl. Its water is whiter than snow and sweeter than honey."

Al-'Awfi narrated something similar from Ibn 'Abbas.

Ibn Jarir said: Ya'qub narrated to me, Hushaym narrated to us, 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib informed us, from Muharib ibn Dithar, from Ibn 'Umar, that he said: "al-Kawthar is a river in Paradise, whose two banks are gold and silver, flowing over pearl and ruby. Its water is far whiter than milk and sweeter than honey."

Likewise al-Tirmidhi narrated it from Ibn Humayd, from Jarir, from 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, with the same, as a statement of a Companion (mawquf). [[Tafsir al-Tabari (30/207). I have not found it in the Sunan of al-Tirmidhi by this route, nor did al-Mizzi mention it in Tuhfat al-Ashraf.]] It has also been reported in marfu' form. Imam Ahmad said:

Ali ibn Hafs narrated to us, Warqa' narrated to us, who said ... and 'Ata' [ibn al-Sa'ib] [addition from M] said, from Muharib ibn Dithar, from Ibn 'Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "al-Kawthar is a river in Paradise, whose two banks are of gold, and the water flows over pearl. Its water is far whiter than milk and sweeter than honey."

This is how al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir narrated it, through the route of Muhammad ibn Fudayl, from 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, with it in marfu' form. [[Al-Musnad (2/158); Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (3361); Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (4334); Tafsir al-Tabari (30/210).]] Al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan sahih."

Ibn Jarir said: Yaqub related to me, Ibn Ulayyah related to us, 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib informed us, saying: Muharib ibn Dithar said to me: "What did Sa'id ibn Jubayr say about al-Kawthar?" I said: "He related to us from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: It is the abundant good." He said: "He spoke the truth; by Allah, it is indeed abundant good. But Ibn 'Umar related to us that he said: When the verse ﴿Indeed, We have granted you al-Kawthar﴾ was revealed, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'al-Kawthar is a river in Paradise, whose banks are of gold, flowing over pearls and rubies.'" [[Tafsir al-Tabari (30/210).]]

Ibn Jarir said: Harun ibn Ishaq related to me, Ibn Abi Maryam related to us, Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn Abi Kathir related to us, Haram ibn 'Uthman informed me, from 'Abd al-Rahman al-A'raj, from Usamah ibn Zayd: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came one day to Hamzah ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib and did not find him, so he asked his wife about him—she was from the Banu al-Najjar—and she said: "O Prophet of Allah, he just went out intending to come to you, and I think he missed you in some of the alleys of the Banu al-Najjar. Will you not enter, O Messenger of Allah?" So he entered, and she brought him a dish of hays, and he ate some of it. She said: "O Messenger of Allah, may it be wholesome and pleasant for you! You came while I was about to come to you to congratulate you and to bring you joy. Abu 'Umarah informed me that you were given a river in Paradise called al-Kawthar." He said: "Indeed, and its expanse—that is, its land—is of rubies, coral, chrysolite and pearls." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (30/210).]]

Haram ibn 'Uthman is weak. However, this context is good, and the basis of this has been authenticated; indeed it has been transmitted through a chain that, according to many of the imams of hadith, yields certainty. Likewise are the hadiths of the Pool [and let us mention them here]. [[An addition from A, and so the Hafiz said; the mention of the hadiths of the Pool does not occur in the copies, but Hafiz Ibn Kathir mentioned them in his book (al-Nihayah fi al-Fitan wa al-Malahim 1/374-412), and were it not for fear of lengthiness we would have mentioned them here, so let it be referred to there.]]

Thus it has been narrated from Anas, Abu al-'Aliyah, Mujahid, and other than one of the early generation (salaf) that al-Kawthar is a river in Paradise. 'Ata' said: it is a pool in Paradise.

* *

His saying: ﴿So pray to your Lord and sacrifice﴾ means: just as We have granted you abundant good in this world and the Hereafter, of which that river whose description has preceded is part—so devote your obligatory prayer and your voluntary prayer to your Lord, and your sacrifice; worship Him alone, with no partner, and sacrifice in His name alone, with no partner. As He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Say: Indeed, my prayer, my rites, my living and my dying are for Allah, Lord of the worlds. He has no partner. And that I have been commanded, and I am the first of the Muslims﴾ [al-An'am: 162-163]. Ibn 'Abbas, 'Ata', Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, and al-Hasan said: this means the sacrifice of camels and the like. Likewise said Qatadah, Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, al-Dahhak, al-Rabi', 'Ata' al-Khurasani, al-Hakam, and Isma'il [in M: "and Sa'id"] ibn Abi Khalid, and other than one of the early generation. This is in contrast to what the polytheists were upon of prostrating to other than Allah and slaughtering in the name of other than Him, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And do not eat of that over which the name of Allah has not been mentioned, for indeed it is grave disobedience﴾ — the verse [al-An'am: 121].

It has been said: what is meant by His saying ﴿and sacrifice﴾ is placing the right hand upon the left beneath the chest (nahr). This is narrated from 'Ali, but it is not authentic. Similarly from al-Sha'bi.

And from Abu Ja'far al-Baqir: ﴿and sacrifice﴾ means: raise the hands at the beginning of the prayer.

It has been said: ﴿and sacrifice﴾ means: face the qiblah with your chest. Ibn Jarir mentioned these three views.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated here a extremely odd hadith, saying: Wahb ibn Ibrahim al-Fami [in A: "al-'Ami"] related to us—in the year 255 AH—Isra'il ibn Hatim al-Marwazi related to us, Muqatil ibn Hayyan related to us, from al-Asbagh ibn Nubatah, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, who said: When this surah was revealed upon the Prophet ﷺ: ﴿Indeed, We have granted you al-Kawthar. So pray to your Lord and sacrifice﴾, the Messenger of Allah said: "O Jibril, what is this sacrifice (nahirah) which my Lord has commanded me with?" He said: "It is not a sacrifice, but He commands you, when you begin the prayer, to raise your hands when you say the takbir, when you bow, when you raise your head from bowing, and when you prostrate, for this is our prayer and the prayer of the angels who are in the seven heavens; and indeed for everything there is an adornment, and the adornment of the prayer is raising the hands at every takbir."

Likewise it was narrated by al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak, from the hadith of Isra'il ibn Hatim, with it. [[al-Mustadrak (2/537); he narrated it also through al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan (2/75); and Ibn Hibban narrated it in al-Majruhin (1/177) through Isra'il ibn Hatim, with it. Ibn Hibban said: "This text is false, except the mention of raising the hands in it; this report was narrated by 'Umar ibn Subh, from Muqatil ibn Hayyan, and 'Umar ibn Subh fabricates hadith, so Isra'il ibn Hatim took advantage of it and narrated it from Muqatil."]]

From 'Ata' al-Khurasani: ﴿and sacrifice﴾ means: raise your back after bowing and stand upright, and expose your chest, meaning by it standing upright (i'tidal). Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim.

[All these views are very odd.] [[An addition from M and A.]] The correct view is the first, that the sacrifice (nahr) means slaughtering the rites (manasik). For this reason the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pray the 'Id and then sacrifice his offering, and he would say: "Whoever prays our prayer and performs our sacrifice, he has done the sacrifice correctly. And whoever sacrifices before the prayer, there is no sacrifice for him." Abu Burdah ibn Niyar stood and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I sacrificed my sheep before the prayer, and I knew that today is a day when meat is desired." He said: "Your sheep is a sheep of meat." He said: "But I have a young female goat (inaq) which is dearer to me than two sheep; will it suffice for me?" He said: "It will suffice you, but it will not suffice anyone after you." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. (983), from the hadith of al-Bara', may Allah be pleased with him.]]

Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir said: The correct view is the statement of the one who said: the meaning of that is: make your entire prayer sincerely for your Lord, to the exclusion of whatever else of rivals and deities [in M: "and children"]; and likewise make your sacrifice for Him alone, to the exclusion of idols; in gratitude to Him for the honour and good which He has given you, which has no equal, and with which He has singled you out. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (30/212).]]

What he said is in the utmost excellence, and Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi and 'Ata' had preceded him to this meaning.

* *

His saying: ﴿Indeed, your hater—he is the one cut off (al-abtar)﴾ means: indeed your hater—O Muhammad—and the hater of what you have brought of guidance, truth, clear proof, shining light and manifest illumination, he is the abtar: the most humble, the most debased, whose remembrance is cut off.

Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, and Qatadah said: it was revealed concerning al-'As ibn Wa'il.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said, from Yazid ibn Ruman, who said: Whenever al-'As ibn Wa'il mentioned the Messenger of Allah ﷺ he would say: "Leave him, for he is an abtar man with no offspring; when he dies, his remembrance will be cut off." So Allah revealed this surah.

Shamir ibn 'Atiyyah said: it was revealed concerning 'Uqbah ibn Abi Mu'ayt.

Ibn 'Abbas also said, as did 'Ikrimah: it was revealed concerning Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf and a group of the disbelievers of Quraysh.

al-Bazzar said: Ziyad ibn Yahya al-Hassani related to us, Ibn Abi 'Adi related to us, from Dawud, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas who said: Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf came to Makkah, and Quraysh said to him: "You are their chief; do you not see this sabir (cut-off one) [in M: 'al-dabr'], the one cut off from his people, who claims he is better than us, while we are the people of the pilgrimage, the keepers of the Ka'bah (sidanah), and the people of the water-providing (siqayah)?" He said: "You are better than him." So it was revealed: ﴿Indeed, your hater—he is the one cut off﴾.

Thus al-Bazzar narrated it [[Musnad al-Bazzar no. (2293), Kashf al-Astar; in it occurs: "al-Hasan ibn 'Ali al-Wasiti related to us, Yahya ibn Rashid related to us, from Dawud," and he mentioned the like; al-Nasa'i also narrated it in al-Sunan al-Kubra no. (11707).]] and its chain is sahih.

And from 'Ata': it was revealed concerning Abu Lahab, at the time when the son of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ died, and Abu Lahab went to the polytheists and said: "Muhammad has been cut off tonight." So Allah revealed concerning that: ﴿Indeed, your hater—he is the one cut off﴾.

And from Ibn 'Abbas: it was revealed concerning Abu Jahl. And from him: ﴿Indeed, your hater﴾ means: your enemy. This encompasses all who are characterized by this among those mentioned, and others.

'Ikrimah said: al-abtar means: the solitary one. al-Suddi said: when a man's male children died, they would say: "He has been cut off." When the sons of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ died, they said: "Muhammad has been cut off." So Allah revealed: ﴿Indeed, your hater—he is the one cut off﴾.

This returns to what we have said, that the abtar is the one whose remembrance is cut off when he dies; they imagined, in their ignorance, that if his sons die, his remembrance is cut off. Far from it, by no means! Rather, Allah has preserved his remembrance upon the heads of witnesses, and has made his law obligatory upon the necks of the servants, continuing through the perpetuity of eternity, until the Day of Gathering and Return, [in M: "and the Day of Calling out"] — the blessings of Allah and His peace be upon him always until the Day of Calling out.

End of the tafsir of Surah "al-Kawthar", and to Allah belongs all praise and grace.
